name: Fraction
doc:
This class implements rational numbers.

In the two-argument form of the constructor, Fraction(8, 6) will
produce a rational number equivalent to 4/3. Both arguments must
be Rational. The numerator defaults to 0 and the denominator
defaults to 1 so that Fraction(3) == 3 and Fraction() == 0.

Fractions can also be constructed from:

  - numeric strings similar to those accepted by the
    float constructor (for example, '-2.3' or '1e10')

  - strings of the form '123/456'

  - float and Decimal instances

  - other Rational instances (including integers)

changed.text: The Fraction constructor now accepts float and decimal.Decimal instances.
The math.gcd() function is now used to normalize the numerator and denominator. math.gcd() always returns an int type. Previously, the GCD type depended on numerator and denominator.
Underscores are now permitted when creating a Fraction instance from a string, following PEP 515 rules.
Fraction implements __int__ now to satisfy typing.SupportsInt instance checks.
Space is allowed around the slash for string inputs: Fraction('2 / 3').
Fraction instances now support float-style formatting, with presentation types "e", "E", "f", "F", "g", "G" and "%"".
Formatting of Fraction instances without a presentation type now supports fill, alignment, sign handling, minimum width and grouping.
The Fraction constructor now accepts any objects with the as_integer_ratio() method.

name: __format__
doc: Format this fraction according to the given format specification.

name: __round__
doc:
round(self, ndigits)

Rounds half toward even.

name: as_integer_ratio
doc:
Return a pair of integers, whose ratio is equal to the original Fraction.

The ratio is in lowest terms and has a positive denominator.

name: denominator
doc: Denominator of the Fraction in lowest terms. Guaranteed to be positive.

name: from_decimal
doc: Converts a finite Decimal instance to a rational number, exactly.

name: from_float
doc:
Converts a finite float to a rational number, exactly.

Beware that Fraction.from_float(0.3) != Fraction(3, 10).

name: from_number
doc:
Converts a finite real number to a rational number, exactly.

Beware that Fraction.from_number(0.3) != Fraction(3, 10).

name: is_integer
doc: Return True if the Fraction is an integer.

name: limit_denominator
doc:
Closest Fraction to self with denominator at most max_denominator.

>>> Fraction('3.141592653589793').limit_denominator(10)
Fraction(22, 7)
>>> Fraction('3.141592653589793').limit_denominator(100)
Fraction(311, 99)
>>> Fraction(4321, 8765).limit_denominator(10000)
Fraction(4321, 8765)

name: numerator
doc: Numerator of the Fraction in lowest term.
